issues: Dolphin body is rendered as a noisy dithered dot-scatter rather than a solid lit phosphor silhouette, which weakens both recognizability and the 'glowing object' read.
Internal fill noise makes the dolphin look like a pointillist/CAD stipple pattern instead of a smooth organic creature; dorsal fin, pectoral fin and tail fluke edges read as muddy clusters of pixels.
Dolphin vertical extent is too small and sits high in the frame; it does not fill the specified middle 50-60% of display height, so dominance is reduced.
Water-surface waveform band is a touch too bright and too tall (looks >15% height) and spans full width, competing with the dolphin for attention.
Bright right-side status text (128BPM / PAR / MIX) is not part of the reference layout and pulls the eye away from the dolphin->text->waves->FFT hierarchy.
Glow halo around the dolphin is weak because the dithering breaks up the edge; the lit-phosphor bloom that should wrap a crisp silhouette is largely missing.
Scattered stray dots around the tail/waterline read as random noise rather than intentional splash or short persistence trails.
suggestions: Fill the dolphin body with a more continuous phosphor brightness and reserve dithering only for internal shading gradients, so the silhouette reads as one solid lit creature.
Add a crisp 1px rim-light outline plus a soft outer bloom halo around the dolphin to sell the 'lit phosphor object' look without blowing out the interior.
Scale the dolphin up and recenter it vertically so its arc occupies roughly 55% of display height, reinforcing it as the absolute centerpiece.
Sharpen anatomical definition: give the dorsal fin a clean triangle, the tail fluke a clear forked crescent, and the pectoral fin a distinct swept shape.
Reduce waveform contrast and clamp its height to <=15% of display height; use thinner, lower-brightness lines so it stays clearly subordinate.
Dim or remove the right-side status text (or move it into the dim FFT/VU tier) so the eye travels dolphin -> top track text -> waves -> FFT as specified.
Replace random stray dots with a deliberate short persistence trail behind the dolphin's motion path (a few fading ghost frames), keeping the rest of the scene clean and unfogged.
Tune overall phosphor response so the dolphin's brightest pixels sit at moderate brightness with a gentle halo, matching a real 1999 OEL panel rather than a flat pixel grid.
